cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) opens with a vineyard let out to husbandmen who will not render the owner his fruit. Paul speaks of the same house in his day: *there is a remnant according to the election of grace*, a chosen part of Yashar'el (Israel) standing where the whole did not.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says a remnant according to the election of grace stands in his own day, a chosen part out of the house.

cards.prose: *The remnant shall return, even the remnant of Jacob*, says Isaiah, and names the chosen part as Jacob's own house. Whatever comes to the husbandmen in the parable, the remnant that survives it is of Jacob and returns unto El Gibbor (the mighty God).
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says the remnant of Jacob shall return to El Gibbor (the mighty God).

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) sends the Sadducees to the bush, where Elohim (God) names himself *the Elohim (God) of Abraham*, of Isaac, and of Jacob. The fathers had been in the ground for generations when he said it, and Yahusha (Jesus) draws the plain conclusion: he is the Elohim (God) of the living, so the fathers are not gone.
cards.member_phrase: I am the Elohim (God) of thy father, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob
cards.member_sentence: At the bush Elohim (God) names himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the words Yahusha (Jesus) brings to the Sadducees.

cards.prose: If the fathers are the living's Elohim (God) in his sense, Daniel says where they are: those who *sleep in the dust of the earth* shall *awake*. Asleep in the dust is how Daniel speaks of the dead, and awake is what is coming to them, in Daniel's own words, the same rising the Sadducees denied.
cards.member_sentence: Daniel says many who sleep in the dust shall awake, some to everlasting life and some to shame and contempt.

cards.prose: *These all died in faith, not having received the promises*, Hebrews says of the fathers, the same fathers Yahusha (Jesus) puts in the bush. They embraced promises they saw only *afar off*, so the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is the Elohim (God) of men who sleep still waiting on what was promised.
cards.member_phrase: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews says the patriarchs died in faith without receiving the promises, having seen them afar off and embraced them.

cards.prose: The scribe says that to love him with all the heart and the neighbour as himself is more than all the offerings. Hosea gave it in the voice of Yahuah (the LORD): *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice*, and the knowledge of Elohim (God) above burnt offerings. The scribe is repeating what the prophets already said.
cards.member_sentence: Hosea says Yahuah (the LORD) desired mercy and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than sacrifice and burnt offerings.

cards.prose: Samuel asked whether Yahuah (the LORD) delights in offerings as much as in being obeyed, and answered, *to obey is better than sacrifice*. The scribe's "more than all whole burnt offerings" is that same ranking, with the obeying of the voice put first.
cards.member_phrase: Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams
cards.member_sentence: Samuel says obeying the voice of Yahuah (the LORD) is better than sacrifice and hearkening than the fat of rams.

cards.prose: Micah asks the question for the scribe: *Wherewith shall I come before Yahuah (LORD)*, with burnt offerings and year-old calves? And answers it as the scribe has just answered Yahusha (Jesus): *to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)* (Micah 6:8).
cards.member_phrase: shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old
cards.member_sentence: Micah asks whether he should come before Yahuah (the LORD) with burnt offerings and calves, and is shown what is good.

new_threads.title: More than all whole burnt offerings — the scribe says what the prophets said
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. A scribe asks which commandment is first, hears the answer, and agrees. Then he goes a step further.

*And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.* (Mark 12:33)

Yahusha (Jesus) says he answered discreetly, and the prophets show why. Hosea had put it in the voice of Yahuah (the LORD) himself.

*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings.* (Hosea 6:6)

Samuel had said it to a king who thought an offering could stand in for hearing.

*And Samuel said, Hath Yahuah (LORD) as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Yahuah (LORD)? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.* (1 Samuel 15:22)

And Micah asks the worshipper's question, how much he must bring.

*Wherewith shall I come before Yahuah (LORD), and bow myself before the high Elohim (God)? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?* (Micah 6:6)

The answer comes a few verses on.

*He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8)

The scribe is not setting the offerings aside, and neither did these three. Each puts the commandment's heart, hearing the voice, mercy, love of Elohim (God) and the neighbour, above the gift laid on the altar, and the scribe says it back to Yahusha (Jesus) in their words.
